paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Mom had good news. "Aunt Sue will arrive tonight," she said, "and she will stay for two days." Aunt Sue was Mom's younger sister, and she lived far away in the north. "She is our guest, so we must make her feel welcome," said Mom. Tom and Lily looked at each other. "I will make a card," said Lily. "And I will do the cooking," said Tom. Dad laughed, but he did not say no.

Lily found some spotted paper in her desk. It was white with small blue spots. She took the scissors and cut the paper into a big heart. Then she wrote "Welcome, Aunt Sue!" in green letters. Pip sat next to her and watched every move. He almost took the scissors, but Lily moved them away. "No, Pip, they are not a toy," she said.

In the afternoon, Dad helped Tom in the kitchen. They made a simple dish with eggs, tomatoes, and green onions. Dad showed him how to break the eggs. Tom cut the onions carefully, and Dad watched. Dad did the hot part on the stove. "Cooking is easy, if you read the steps," said Tom. Soon the kitchen smelled delicious, and Pip ran in. "Not yet, Pip!" said Dad. Pip sat down, but he did not look away from the food.

Aunt Sue arrived at six o'clock. Mom opened the door, and Aunt Sue came in with a big bag. Pip ran around her legs and barked. "Hello, everybody!" she said. Lily gave her the card, and Aunt Sue smiled. "It is lovely," she said, "and I like the blue spots." "Please hurry," said Tom. "If you don't hurry, the dish will get cold."

They all sat around the table. Aunt Sue ate a piece and said, "It is delicious!" Tom smiled, but he said nothing. "Who made it?" she asked. "Tom and Dad did," said Lily, "but I made the card, so I helped, too." Aunt Sue laughed and said, "Then everybody in this house is a good cook!" Pip sat under the table and waited.
